description: Use this tool whenever a user needs cash liquidity (for a real estate purchase bridge, tax bill, tuition, or business investment) and asks whether they should sell appreciated stocks/ETFs (paying capital gains tax gross-up) or borrow against their portfolio using a Securities-Backed Line of Credit (SBLOC), Schwab Pledged Asset Line (PAL), or margin loan. Computes the tax gross-up penalty, break-even borrowing interest rate, IRC Sec. 163(d) Form 4952 interest deduction, and LTV market-crash margin call buffer.

interestDeductible.description: True if loan proceeds are traced to a taxable investment or business purpose eligible for IRC Sec. 163(d) Form 4952 deduction.

liquidityNeeded.description: Net after-tax cash liquidity required in USD.

loanYears.description: Number of years the bridge loan / SBLOC will remain outstanding.

marginalOrdinaryRate.description: Marginal ordinary federal bracket percentage for Form 4952 deduction.

marketReturn.description: Expected annual portfolio return percentage while invested.

portfolioCostBasis.description: Total original cost basis of the taxable portfolio in USD.

portfolioValue.description: Total taxable brokerage portfolio market value in USD.

sblocRate.description: Annual SBLOC / Pledged Asset Line interest rate percentage (e.g. 6.25).

stateRatePct.description: State capital gains tax rate percentage (0 for TX/FL/NV).

name: compare_sbloc_borrow_vs_sell
title: Compare Selling Appreciated Investments vs. Borrowing via SBLOC / Pledged Asset Line
